purpose: Per-topic target quotas for building a question BANK/dataset, not a simulation of a single adaptive session. Multiply/scale as needed. Mirrors the structure of the JEE Main quotas file so banks across exams can be planned/compared side by side.
question_type_note: GMAT Focus Edition uses 5-option single-correct MCQ ('Problem Solving') in Quant, 5-option single-correct MCQ in Verbal (Reading Comprehension and Critical Reasoning), and five distinct interactive formats in Data Insights (Data Sufficiency MCQ, Table Analysis true/false grid, Graphics Interpretation dropdown-completion, Two-Part Analysis linked-answer table, Multi-Source Reasoning tabbed MCQ/true-false). There is no numerical-value entry format like JEE's Section B anywhere on the GMAT.
difficulty_note: GMAT does not expose fixed easy/medium/hard question slots to candidates — the live exam is section-adaptive and picks difficulty question-by-question based on the test-taker's running performance. For question-bank seeding purposes this file still tags each item with a target difficulty band (low/medium/high), matching how prep providers and the adaptive engine's internal item-difficulty parameters are commonly described, so that a bank can supply items across the full difficulty range the algorithm might draw from.

Q01.notes: Number Properties and Ratios/Percent/Interest are consistently among the most frequently tested arithmetic areas.

Q02.notes: Linear & Quadratic Equations is reported as the single largest Quant sub-area by several trackers (~29% of the section).

V01.notes: Passages typically 200-350 words; 3-4 questions per passage in real exam delivery, but for bank-seeding purposes items are pooled by skill rather than by passage.

V02.notes: Assumption, strengthen/weaken and inference sub-types are the most heavily recurring archetypes.

DI01.notes: Most frequent single DI question type; estimates across sources range 20-40% of the section (roughly 6-8 of the 20 live questions).

DI02.notes: Reported at roughly 10-20% of the section (~3-4 of 20 live questions).

DI03.notes: Reported at roughly 20-30% of the section (~4-5 of 20 live questions), the second-most frequent DI type after Data Sufficiency.

DI04.notes: Reported at roughly 10-20% of the section (~2-3 of 20 live questions).

DI05.notes: Reported at roughly 10-20% of the section (~2-3 of 20 live questions); each MSR prompt commonly yields 2-3 linked questions in the live exam, pooled here as individual bank items.
